content:
Dr. Maya Srinivasan: Hey all — quick request from Applied ML on the hardware profile workload matrix. Current prompt distributions in the perf suite feel too “clean”. We’re not seeing tool-calling patterns, multi-turn chat formatting, or the long-tail of prefill lengths we get in production. That’s going to overstate wins for some scheduler/kernel knobs and miss regressions.

Claire Dubois: +1, we’ve been using mostly single-turn, mostly uniform seq-len buckets for reproducibility. What specifically do you want to see represented?

Arjun Desai: A few concrete things:
- prompt length mix should be skewed (tons of short prompts, some medium, small but important tail of long-context)
- include “chatty” wrappers (system + user + assistant turns), not just raw user text
- tool calling: JSON/function-call style outputs + tool result injection back into context (prefill spikes)
- streaming: we should validate TTFT and steady-state tokens/sec separately. Some of the H100 “throughput” presets look great on non-streaming but we’ve seen jitter in streaming decode.

Jonas Weber: Also: output length distributions. Right now we cap decode pretty aggressively in the suite, which hides tail latency and KV cache pressure. Even just a mixed target (e.g., 64/256/1024 output tokens) would be better.

Rina Kobayashi: This makes sense. Biggest blocker historically is: we can’t use real customer prompts, and “synthetic” quickly gets subjective. If we have a principled spec (histograms/mixture weights), we can generate prompts from a pinned corpus.

Sofia Ivanova: From scheduling POV, the suite currently under-weights the nasty cases:
- multi-turn with a big tool result blob
- mixed concurrency where some requests are short (chat) and some are long (RAG)
Those are exactly where prefill/decode fairness + backpressure changes show up as p95 spikes.

Marcus Reed: +1. We just fixed a fairness regression (PR-22033). Would’ve been caught earlier with a more realistic mix.

Dr. Maya Srinivasan: Totally. We’re not asking to stuff in customer data. We can give you distributions from aggregated production metrics (no content):
- prefill token histogram (p50/p90/p95/p99)
- ratio of tool-calling requests by route (roughly)
- streaming usage %
And then build a synthetic generator to match those stats.

Noah Patel: We should do this, but carefully: benchmark suite must remain deterministic. If we add a generator, it must be seedable + stable across runs.

Claire Dubois: Proposal:
1) define a “realistic mix” workload scenario in the matrix alongside the existing clean buckets
2) keep it content-free: use a pinned prompt set with templated wrappers + a pinned “tool result blob” fixture
3) enforce mixture weights in the runner (benchmark-lab PR-1842 runner can sample deterministically)

Arjun Desai: That’s exactly what we want. For the tool result blob: we should include a couple sizes (e.g., 2KB, 20KB, 200KB equivalent tokens), since some customers shove big retrieval results or tables.

Omar El-Sayed: Heads up: 200KB-ish blobs will blow up KV cache fast on L40S unless we set stricter KV budgeting. But… that’s kinda the point; we need to exercise the guardrails.

Samir Qureshi: For L40S in particular, we should include at least one “long-context + medium decode” case at moderate concurrency to trigger fragmentation patterns. The earlier OOMs were not showing up in the existing matrix.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel side: if we add chat wrappers + tool-call JSON, we also want to ensure we’re not accidentally biasing tokenization patterns to something pathological. But ok — as long as it’s representative and pinned.

Rina Kobayashi: Can someone from Applied ML provide the mixture targets? Even rough:
- % short/med/long prefill
- % tool-call
- % streaming
- typical max_new_tokens buckets

Jonas Weber: I can post a draft by EOD. Rough starting point (based on what we see in eval harness + what Maya mentioned):
- Prefill: 60% (<=512), 25% (513–2k), 10% (2k–8k), 5% (8k–32k)
- Output: 50% (<=128), 35% (129–512), 15% (513–2048)
- Tool-call: 12–18% depending on route; we can start with 15%
- Streaming: 70% streaming / 30% non-streaming for chat routes; but suite-level maybe 50/50 to keep coverage.

Sofia Ivanova: Please also make sure the streaming runs record:
- TTFT p50/p95
- inter-token latency p95
- “stall” rate (gaps > X ms)
We’ve had configs that improve aggregate tok/s but degrade perceived UX.

Claire Dubois: Agree. We currently report p50/p95 end-to-end. We can extend the artifact schema to include TTFT + decode jitter for streaming cases.

Marcus Reed: Implementation detail: the runner can do two passes per scenario: one streaming, one non-streaming. Same prompts, different transport, and we compare.

Dr. Maya Srinivasan: That’s good. Another nuance: tool calling often means structured output constraints. Even if we don’t validate correctness, we should at least shape outputs like JSON-ish so token patterns match.

Hiro Tanaka: We can add a “structured output” prompt template (e.g., “Return JSON with keys …”) + a fixed validator disabled. It’ll still drive the model into the right mode.

Noah Patel: Let’s capture scope so it doesn’t balloon:
- v1: mixture weights + templates + fixed tool blob fixtures + streaming metrics
- later: add correctness checks / eval scoring if needed

Talia Benson: Can we turn this into a specific action item for ENG-4827 / ENG-4829? This seems like a dependency for “expected behavior” docs too.

Claire Dubois: Yep, I’ll add a subtask on ENG-4827 (workload matrix) and tag Applied ML for the distributions.

Rina Kobayashi: I’ll take the runner changes (deterministic sampling + new scenario definition). Will coordinate with Kira V. on how this impacts perf-canary noise.

Arjun Desai: Thanks. One more ask: please keep the “clean buckets” scenario too. We still need micro-style coverage for isolating kernel changes.

Sofia Ivanova: +1, keep both. Clean buckets for diagnosis, realistic mix for guardrails.

Dr. Maya Srinivasan: Perfect. I’ll send the aggregated histogram summary + suggested mixture to Claire/Rina. Appreciate the quick turn.

Marcus Reed: :thumbsup: once this lands, we should rerun H100 balanced vs throughput-first on the realistic mix. I suspect we’ll see the tail trade-offs more clearly.

Talia Benson: Great. I’ll note in weekly sync that “realistic mix scenario” is now part of acceptance for the profile pack release.
